title: Invertibility of the native lisse adic bidual map
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime and $X$ any scheme [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R$ be the native adic coefficient ring sheaf, and let $M$ be an $R$-module sheaf in the native internal-module presentation [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume $M$ is pro-etale locally isomorphic to a finite direct sum of copies of the regular module, with ranks allowed to vary. Put $D(M)=\mathcal Hom_R(M,R)$. The actual native map $\delta_M:M\to D(D(M))$ of [lem-sf-adic-native-bidual], defined by transposing $1_{D(M)}$, is an isomorphism. No Frobenius structure or arithmetic base field is part of this statement.

source.place: Finite-free bidual evaluation is the identity, followed by locality and stability under restriction.

proof.text: Obtain the native/slice comparison P from [lem-sf-adic-module-slice-hom-comparison]. At any base, compose its Hom comparison with its regular-module comparison to get an isomorphism from the image of the native dual to the sectionwise dual; apply the same construction again contravariantly to get the double-dual comparison. The bidual_sections and evaluation fields, together with section_map and section_restriction, show on each further slice that the transported bidual sends x to the functional lambda ↦ lambda(x restricted). Uncurrying and bidual_transpose identify P.bidual with the named adicNativeBidual of [lem-sf-adic-native-bidual].

proof.text: For a module isomorphic to a finite sum of regular modules, use the equivalence and its freeIso to obtain a sectionwise free module. Write its coordinate inclusions s_i and projections c_i; their total sum is the identity. On every slice, x = sum_i c_i(x) s_i(1), so evaluation into the double dual is injective. A double-dual section Psi is evaluation at sum_i Psi(c_i) s_i(1): express each local functional as the sum of its basis values times the restrictions of the c_i, and use naturality and commutativity of the coefficient ring. This proves surjectivity. The empty sum handles rank zero. This is the finite dual-basis proof of PresheafOfModules.bidual_app_bijective, written privately with independent object and morphism universes and for a supplied evaluation map. Componentwise inverses form a presheaf isomorphism by PresheafOfModules.isoMk; reflect it through the fully faithful forgetful functor and P.E to prove P.bidual invertible for each finite-free native module.

proof.text: Choose the pro-etale covering family in the definition of lisse and its finite-free trivializations. On each member apply the preceding finite-free calculation at that base. The bidual_slice equation of [lem-sf-adic-module-slice-hom-comparison] identifies the pullback of P.bidual, up to the two canonical invertible native-dual comparison maps, with this invertible local bidual. Thus its pullbacks are invertible. Apply the already proved ProEtale.isIso_of_isIso_localizationRestriction to the underlying coefficient-vector-space sheaf, using upperStarIsoLocalizationRestriction and NatIso.isIso_map_iff to identify the maps. The underlying-sheaf functor reflects isomorphisms. Finally replace P.bidual by adicNativeBidual using its transpose characterization. This is exactly the finite-free evaluation and locality route, with no uniform rank or points.
